title: Annotatio III §.I: Chytraeus on Zwingli/Oecolampadius follow Luther elsewhere; interim Christian love; Buddeus Luther to Agricola; wish bitterness eased
pass_a_gloss: On which matter Chytraeus thus: Zwingli and Oecolampadius willingly followed Luther’s Sentence in all the rest; on the Sacrament alone they refused to follow, p. 643. Although, however, whether the true Body and Blood of Christ be Corporally present in the Bread and Wine of the Lord’s Supper we have not agreed at this time, yet one party will declare Christian love to the other as far as each one’s Conscience will bear, and both parties will diligently pray God Almighty that He confirm us by His Spirit in the true Sentence, p. 646. The most distinguished Buddeus, the celebrated Halle Professor, adds in the Supplement Luther’s Epistle 98 addressed to Johann Agricola, persuasive that thereafter all harsh words and Writings should cease, pp. 71–72. Chytraeus himself moreover testifies at the start of his History of the Acts with the Zwinglians that he with all the pious wishes the bitterness of dissensions and hatreds be softened and mitigated, p. 636.
pass_b_english: On that outcome Chytraeus writes: Zwingli and Oecolampadius gladly followed Luther’s teaching in everything else; only on the Sacrament they would not follow (p. 643).

Though they had not yet agreed whether Christ’s true body and blood are corporally present in the bread and wine of the Lord’s Supper, each side would still show the other Christian love as far as conscience allowed, and both would pray God to confirm them by His Spirit in the true teaching (p. 646).
Buddeus, the noted Halle professor, adds in his Supplement Luther’s Epistle 98 to Johann Agricola, urging that harsh words and writings stop from then on (pp. 71–72).
Chytraeus himself, opening his History of the Acts with the Zwinglians, says he and all the pious wish the bitterness of these splits and hatreds softened and eased (p. 636).
source_text: Qua de re ita Chytraeus: Zwinglius & Oecolampadius libenter, in caeteris omnibus, Lutheri Sententiam secuti sunt, de Sacramento tantùm sequi noluerunt p. 643. Etsi autem, an verum Corpus & Sanguis Christi Corporaliter in Pane & Vino Coenae Domini praesens sit, hoc tempore non concordavimus, tamen una pars alteri Christianam dilectionem, quantum cujusq; Conscientia feret, declarabit, & utraque pars Deum Omnipotentem diligenter orabit, ut nos Spiritu suo in vera Sententia confirmet, pag. 646. Addit Clariss. Buddeus, Prof. Hallensis celeberrimus, in Supplemento, Epistolam Lutheri 98. Joh. Agricolae inscriptam suasoriam quò omnia aspera verba & Scripta cessarent in posterum pag. 71. 72. Ipse praetereà Chytraeus contestatur initio Hist. suae de Actis cum Zwingl. secum omnibus piis optare, quò dissidiorum odiorumq; acerbitas leniatur & mitigetur. pag. 636.
